title: Build pressure on an absolute pin
text: The rook on d5 is pinned to the king by Bf3. After ...Kc6, Bxd5+ only wins the exchange and lets Black recapture. White can instead play c4, attacking the pinned rook again and winning it outright.

title: A pinned defender cannot stop mate
text: The knight on g8 shields its king from the rook but is pinned. Qh6 is mate: neither the knight nor the queen on g7 can capture it without exposing the king.

title: Check the opponent’s reply
text: White has played Rg4 to attack the knight pinned to the king. Black replies ...Bh5, pinning the attacking rook to White’s king and turning the tables.

title: A relative pin can be broken
text: The f6 knight is pinned to the queen, not the king. Nxd5 is a mistake: Black answers ...Nxd5, allows Bxd8, then uses ...Bb4+ and ...Bxd2+ before recovering the queen. White ends a piece down.
demonstration: Nxd5 Nxd5 Bxd8 Bb4+ Qd2 Bxd2+ Kxd2 Kxd8

title: Unpin by attacking the bishop
text: The c6 knight is pinned and attacked by d5, but ...a6 drives the bishop to a4 and ...b5 attacks it again. After dxc6, ...bxa4 recovers a piece; after Bb3, ...Na5 releases the knight. Examine these active defenses before spending time preventing every pin.
